symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The length of the source transform, the number of coordinates it acts on.
symbols.quote: Gaussian resampling rewrites a Fourier transform of length $s$, the number of its coordinates, as a transform with target length $t>s$ and power-of-two axis lengths, keeping the source and target coordinate permutations inside the identity.

symbols.name: target length
symbols.meaning: The target length, the number of coordinates of the longer transform.
symbols.quote: Gaussian resampling rewrites a Fourier transform of length $s$, the number of its coordinates, as a transform with target length $t>s$ and power-of-two axis lengths, keeping the source and target coordinate permutations inside the identity.

symbols.name: Gaussian width
symbols.meaning: A fixed integer that sets the width of the Gaussian weights.
symbols.quote: Let $\alpha\ge2$ be a fixed integer, the Gaussian width.

symbols.name: normalized transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform of length $q$, mapping a vector of length $q$ to one of length $q$.
symbols.quote: Let $F_q$ be the normalized transform of length $q$, $(F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2\pi i jk/q}$.

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation of length-$s$ vectors that sends $u$ to the vector with entries $u_{tj}$.
symbols.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the maps $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, where $u$ has length $s$, $v$ has length $t$ (here $v$ is new, not its earlier meaning), and indices are taken modulo $s$ and $t$.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation of length-$t$ vectors that sends $v$ to the vector with entries $v_{-sk}$.
symbols.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the maps $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, where $u$ has length $s$, $v$ has length $t$ (here $v$ is new, not its earlier meaning), and indices are taken modulo $s$ and $t$.

symbols.name: target vector
symbols.meaning: A vector of length $t$, the input to the target permutation $P_t$.
symbols.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the maps $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, where $u$ has length $s$, $v$ has length $t$ (here $v$ is new, not its earlier meaning), and indices are taken modulo $s$ and $t$.

symbols.name: Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: The map from length $s$ to length $t$ whose $k$-th output is a Gaussian-weighted sum centred at $sk/t$.
symbols.quote: $G$ is the map whose $k$-th output is a Gaussian-weighted sum centred at $sk/t$, and $T$ weights each input $u_j$ by a Gaussian centred at $tj/s$:

symbols.name: dual Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: The map from length $s$ to length $t$ that weights each input $u_j$ by a Gaussian centred at $tj/s$.
symbols.quote: $G$ is the map whose $k$-th output is a Gaussian-weighted sum centred at $sk/t$, and $T$ weights each input $u_j$ by a Gaussian centred at $tj/s$:

symbols.name: weight map
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map on length-$s$ vectors that multiplies entry $j$ by $e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}$.
symbols.quote: Let $E$ multiply entry $j$ by $e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}$, where $q_j=\lfloor tj/s+\tfrac12\rfloor$ is the integer nearest $tj/s$ (ties rounded up) and $\beta_j=tj/s-q_j$, so $|\beta_j|\le\tfrac12$.

symbols.name: nearest index
symbols.meaning: The integer nearest $tj/s$, rounding ties up, which is the target coordinate that $C$ selects for index $j$.
symbols.quote: Let $E$ multiply entry $j$ by $e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}$, where $q_j=\lfloor tj/s+\tfrac12\rfloor$ is the integer nearest $tj/s$ (ties rounded up) and $\beta_j=tj/s-q_j$, so $|\beta_j|\le\tfrac12$.

symbols.name: rounding offset
symbols.meaning: The signed distance $tj/s-q_j$ from $tj/s$ to its nearest integer, with absolute value at most $\tfrac12$.
symbols.quote: Let $E$ multiply entry $j$ by $e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}$, where $q_j=\lfloor tj/s+\tfrac12\rfloor$ is the integer nearest $tj/s$ (ties rounded up) and $\beta_j=tj/s-q_j$, so $|\beta_j|\le\tfrac12$.

symbols.name: selection map
symbols.meaning: The map from length $t$ to length $s$ that selects the coordinates $v_{q_j}$.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ map $\mathbb C^t$ to $\mathbb C^s$ by $(Cv)_j=v_{q_j}$, and let $N=CTE$, a map from $\mathbb C^s$ to itself.

symbols.name: near-identity map
symbols.meaning: The composite map $CTE$ on length-$s$ vectors, which is close to the identity.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ map $\mathbb C^t$ to $\mathbb C^s$ by $(Cv)_j=v_{q_j}$, and let $N=CTE$, a map from $\mathbb C^s$ to itself.

symbols.name: identity map
symbols.meaning: The identity map on vectors, the operator with $Iu=u$.
symbols.quote: The Neumann series $\sum_{m\ge0}(I-N)^m$, where $I$ is the identity map, converges to $N^{-1}$ when $\|I-N\|<\tfrac12$, so $\|N^{-1}\|\le2$.

symbols.name: first contraction
symbols.meaning: The contraction $R=\tfrac12 G$ from length $s$ to length $t$.
symbols.quote: Let $R=\tfrac12G$ and $Q=2^{1-2\alpha^2}EN^{-1}C$, with $R$ mapping $\mathbb C^s$ to $\mathbb C^t$ and $Q$ mapping back.

symbols.name: second contraction
symbols.meaning: The contraction $Q=2^{1-2\alpha^2}EN^{-1}C$ from length $t$ back to length $s$.
symbols.quote: Let $R=\tfrac12G$ and $Q=2^{1-2\alpha^2}EN^{-1}C$, with $R$ mapping $\mathbb C^s$ to $\mathbb C^t$ and $Q$ mapping back.

Thus Gaussian resampling expresses each source transform through a [Multidimensional transform with power-of-two axes](multidim-transform.md).
